passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (MD&A) is designed to provide a reader of 3M’s financial statements with a narrative from the perspective of management. 3M’s MD&A is presented in the following sections: • Overview • Results of Operations • Performance by Business Segment • Performance by Geographic Area • Critical Accounting Estimates • New Accounting Pronouncements • Financial Condition and Liquidity • Financial Instruments Forward-looking statements in Item 7 may involve risks and uncertainties that could cause results to differ materially from those projected (refer to the section entitled Cautionary Note Concerning Factors That May Affect Future Results in Item 1 and the risk factors provided in Item 1A for discussion of these risks and uncertainties). Additional information about results of operations and financial condition for 2024 and 2023 (including the detailed discussion of the prior year 2024 to 2023 year-over-year changes) can be found in Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations sections in 3M's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024. Table of Contents Overview 3M is a diversified global manufacturer, technology innovator and marketer of a wide variety of products and services. As discussed in Note 1, certain changes are reflective in this document for all applicable periods presented. As discussed in Note 2, on April 1, 2024, 3M completed the separation of its Health Care business (the Separation) through a pro rata distribution of 80.1% of the outstanding shares of Solventum Corporation (Solventum) to 3M stockholders. As a result, Solventum became an independent public company, 3M no longer consolidated Solventum into 3M’s financial results and the historical net income of Solventum, and applicable assets and liabilities included in the Separation were reported in 3M's consolidated financial statements as discontinued operations. 3M manages its continuing operations in three operating business segments: Safety and Industrial; Transportation and Electronics; and Consumer. From a geographic perspective, EMEA refers to Europe, the Middle East, and Africa on a combined basis. Unless otherwise noted, any sales change analysis compares 2025 with 2024, year-on-year (YoY). passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Provided below is a cautionary discussion of what we believe to be the most important risk factors applicable to the Company. Discussion of these factors is incorporated by reference into and considered an integral part of Part II, Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.” Risks Related to the Global Economy and External Conditions * The Company’s results are impacted by the effects of, and changes in, worldwide economic, political, regulatory, international trade, geopolitical, tariffs and retaliatory counter measures, and other external conditions. During 2025, the Company derived approximately 56 percent of its revenues from outside the United States. Accordingly, the Company’s operations and the execution of its business strategies and plans are subject to global competition and economic and geopolitical risks that are beyond its control, such as, among other things, disruptions in financial markets, economic downturns, military conflicts, terrorism, public health emergencies, political changes and trends such as protectionism, economic nationalism resulting in government actions impacting international trade agreements or imposing trade restrictions such as tariffs and retaliatory counter measures, and government deficit reduction and other austerity measures in locations or industries in which the Company operates. Further escalation of specific trade tensions, including those between the U.S. and China, or more broadly in global trade conflict, could have a material adverse effect on the Company's business and operations around the world. The Company's business is also impacted by social, political, and labor conditions in locations in which the Company or its suppliers or customers operate; adverse changes in the availability and cost of capital; monetary policy; interest rates; inflation; recession; commodity prices; currency volatility or exchange control; ability to expatriate earnings; and other laws and regulations in the jurisdictions in which the Company or its suppliers or customers operate. For example, changes in local economic condition or outlooks, such as lower economic growth rates in China, Europe, or other key markets, impact the demand or profitability of the Company's products. The global economy has been impacted by geopolitical tensions. The U.S. and other governments have imposed, and propose to impose additional, export controls and tariffs on certain products, and financial and economic sanctions on certain industry sectors and parties. These geopolitical tensions could result in, among other things, cyberattacks, supply chain disruptions (including limitations on access to rare earth minerals and other raw materials), higher energy and other commodity costs, lower consumer demand, and changes to foreign exchange rates and financial markets, and tariffs and trade restrictions may result in increased production costs and product pricing, further supply chain disruptions, limited access to end markets, lower profitability, and uncertainty related to planning long-term investments and strategies, and may have other competitive effects. credit_strengths.text: Gross leverage sits below the sector median on a like-for-like definition, and net leverage is also comfortably under the sector median, reflecting a debt stock reduced over successive years while the EBITDA proxy held broadly steady. This positions the issuer in the stronger half of its peer group on balance-sheet gearing.

Operating margin is modestly above the sector median, and interest coverage improved year on year, indicating that core manufacturing profitability is adequate to carry the fixed charge burden. Coverage nonetheless remains below the sector median, so the advantage is one of gearing rather than earnings power.

key_risks.text: The issuer derives a majority of revenue from outside the United States, so tariffs, retaliatory counter measures, trade tension and currency volatility are direct earnings risks. Escalating trade conflict could raise input costs, disrupt supply chains and compress margins, which would erode the headroom currently held against the next leverage band.

The debt note shows a large current portion of long-term debt falling due within the next year alongside fixed-rate notes maturing across the following decades, so refinancing is a recurring funding task. Floating-rate exposure was reduced by terminating swaps, but the near-term maturity wall still requires market access at acceptable coupons.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow covers the dividend but falls short of capital expenditure plus dividends, and is well below buybacks and total shareholder distributions. Free cash flow likewise falls short of dividends, buybacks and aggregate distributions, so the shareholder return programme is not fully self-funded from internally generated cash.

Cash flow to debt improved year on year yet remains below the sector median, and free cash flow to debt, while better than the prior year, is also below peers. Coverage of interest and EBITDA exceeds unity with margin, but the cash conversion profile is the weaker leg of the credit story.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is Intermediate, driven by the weaker of leverage and cash flow. Leverage sits in the lowest tier with meaningful headroom before the next band, whereas cash flow sits in a higher tier close to its boundary, so a modest EBITDA decline would move the assessment before gearing did.

Our forward view is that gearing remains supportable given the reduced debt stock and solid liquidity, but distributions exceeding free cash flow and external trade exposure temper the trajectory. We would look for free cash flow coverage of distributions to improve before viewing deleveraging as self-funding rather than balance-sheet dependent.

credit_strengths.text: 按同類比較基準計算，總槓桿低於行業中位數，淨槓桿亦穩妥地低於行業中位數，反映債務存量於連續數年內下降，而 EBITDA 代理指標大致保持穩定。此使發行人在同業組別中處於資產負債表槓桿較強的一半。
營業利潤率略高於行業中位數，利息覆蓋率按年改善，顯示核心製造盈利能力足以承擔固定費用負擔。然而覆蓋率仍低於行業中位數，故此優勢在於槓桿而非盈利能力。

key_risks.text: 發行人大部分收入來自美國以外地區，因此關稅、報復性反制措施、貿易緊張及貨幣波動均為直接盈利風險。貿易衝突升級可能推高投入成本、擾亂供應鏈並壓縮利潤率，從而侵蝕目前相對於下一槓桿區間所持有的緩衝。
債務附註顯示大量長期債務的流動部分將於未來一年內到期，同時固定利率票據將於其後數十年陸續到期，故再融資是一項經常性的融資任務。浮動利率風險因終止掉期而降低，但近期到期牆仍須以可接受票息進入市場融資。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 經營現金流覆蓋股息，但不足以覆蓋資本開支加股息，並遠低於回購及股東分派總額。自由現金流同樣不足以覆蓋股息、回購及分派總額，故股東回報計劃並非完全由內部產生現金自給自足。
現金流對債務比率按年改善，但仍低於行業中位數；自由現金流對債務比率雖優於上年，亦低於同業。利息及 EBITDA 覆蓋率以一定幅度超過一，但現金轉換狀況是信用故事中較弱的一環。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為 Intermediate，由槓桿及現金流中較弱的一項所驅動。槓桿處於最低級別，距下一區間有顯著緩衝；而現金流處於較高級別且接近其邊界，故 EBITDA 溫和下降將先於槓桿變動而改變評估。
我們的前瞻觀點是，鑑於債務存量減少及流動性穩健，槓桿仍屬可支持，但分派超過自由現金流及外部貿易敞口令軌跡受限。我們會期望自由現金流對分派的覆蓋改善後，才視去槓桿為自給自足而非依賴資產負債表。
